scenes.heading: Building a repeatable workflow from inquiry to delivery

sents.d: Building a repeatable workflow from inquiry to delivery
A clear process reduces stress and makes you look more professional.
Without a defined workflow, every new inquiry becomes a fresh decision about what to send, when to follow up, and how to structure the shoot — which wastes time and creates room for mistakes.

A simple repeatable sequence works well for most videographers: initial inquiry response within 24 hours, a short discovery call or questionnaire, a written proposal with pricing, a signed contract and deposit, a pre-shoot planning call, the shoot itself, an editing and review period with a defined number of revisions, and final delivery with a request for a testimonial.

scenes.heading: Write it down so it never slips

sents.d: Writing this sequence down — even as a simple checklist — means you can hand parts of it off to an assistant or virtual assistant later, and it prevents steps like contracts or deposits from being skipped when you're busy or excited about a new client.

take: Write down your inquiry-to-delivery steps and follow them every time.
